- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.3) and forecast is trending up, reduce upward bias by 5–10% to avoid overcorrection.  
- If sentiment turns negative (≤ -0.2) and forecast is high, apply downward pressure: subtract 3–5% from peak forecasts.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75), model tends to overshoot; cap forecast at +10% above prior peak or adjust downward by 2–3 points if sentiment is neutral or negative.  
- If sentiment is consistently low (≤ 0.1) over 3+ days, model overestimates mean; apply mean reversion by subtracting 2–4% from forecasted values.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often overpredicts early in the window; reduce first 5–7 days’ forecast by 1–3% if sentiment is weak or neutral.  
- If sentiment is high but price drops sharply in next 3–5 days, model tends to lag; adjust forecast downward by 1–2% for the next 3–5 days.
